mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, which reduces equity discount rates and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Rising FOMC rates in late-cycle inflationary environment
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) after a FEDFUNDS increase of ≥0.25%, or inflation surprises are not consistent with the rate hike.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) coinciding with a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) predicts stronger consumer demand and supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Labor market tightening before a recovery phase
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat, or the PAYEMS/UNRATE relationship reverses in the following quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in GDPC1 (real private demand) of at least 3% for two consecutive months is associated with stronger corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > prev(GDPC1) * 1.03 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive after the two-month GDPC1 acceleration, or earnings revisions turn negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% in a month is interpreted as supply-side weakness, lowering growth expectations and producing negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Supply shock or contraction in a recovery phase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite INDPRO contraction, or the effect reverses in the next month.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months, the expectation of sustained easing supports higher equity valuations and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1) or FEDFUNDS rises above 2% in the next month without further positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% combined with a decline in HOUST (housing starts) signals labor market softening and reduced consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 20-day returns.
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market cooling
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative or the UNRATE/HOUST relationship reverses within the next 30 days.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 8% in a month, it indicates weak consumer demand and a higher probability of negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Retail demand contraction in a growth slowdown
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive despite the RSAFS decline, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 4% for a month triggers a risk-off reaction, lowering equity valuations and producing negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: High-inflation surprise in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative or inflation decelerates rapidly within the next two months.
